## Shadows
```
ShadowMesh -> ShadowMeshIndex -> ShadowMeshOpaqueVertex
          \-> MaterialSort   \-> ShadowMeshAlphaVertex
```
### Titanfall 2
```
ShadowEnvironment -> ShadowMesh
                 \-> CSMAABBNodes -> CSMObjReferences
                                                   
ShadowEnvironments are indexed by entities (light_environment(_volume) w/ lightEnvironmentIndex key)
```

## CSM (Cascading Shadow Maps)
```
CSMAABBNode -> CSMObjReference -> ??? (starts high, out of ObjRefs range)
           \-> CSMAABBNode
```

## LightProbe
```
LightProbeTree -?> LightProbeRef -> LightProbe

StaticPropLightProbeIndices & StaticProps are parallel
```
### Titanfall 2
```
-?> LightProbeBSPNodes -> ???
                  \-> LightProbeBspNodes

-?> LightProbeBSPRefIds -?>

-?> LightProbeParentInfos -?>
```

## World Lights
```
WorldLight -> TextureData
          \-> Entities (parent)
```
### Titanfall 2
```
WorldLight -> TextureData
          \-?> WorldLightParentInfos
```

nodes.body:
CSM must help w/ optimising real time shadows in some way
Has a node tree, might flag some meshes which cast shadows?
`CSMObjRefs` is a real mystery atm

Might help to get the bounds of leaves (`CSMAABBNodes` w/ no child `Nodes` / child `ObjRefs`)

`LightProbeBspNodes` have a `plane` embedded in them (not an index!)
The also appear to have 2 `int32_t` indices (likely `front` & `back` of `plane`)
`-ve` indices are huge and could be a bitfield?

```python
>>> [n.children for n in bsp.LIGHTPROBE_BSP_NODES[:16]]
[(1, 3181), (2, 1633), (3, 753), (4, 499),
 (5, 189), (6, 129), (7, 121), (8, 60),
 (9, 59), (10, 57), (11, 54), (12, 24),
 (13, -1879048087), (14, 15),
 (-1946157056, -1744830458), (-1778384878, 16)]
>>> hex(-1879048087)
'-0x6fffff97'
>>> (-1879048087).to_bytes(4, "little", signed=True)
b'i\x00\x00\x90'  # bitfield?
```

```python
>>> indices = {n.unknown[0] for n in bsp.LIGHTPROBE_BSP_NODES}.union({n.unknown[1] for n in bsp.LIGHTPROBE_BSP_NODES})
>>> indices == {*range(1, len(bsp.LIGHTPROBE_BSP_NODES))}
False
>>> indices2 = {i for i in indices if 0 < i < len(bsp.LIGHTPROBE_BSP_NODES)}
>>> indices2 == {*range(1, len(bsp.LIGHTPROBE_BSP_NODES))}
True
```

Haven't looked at `WorldLight.parent` yet
There's a lot of neat world light default overrides in `engine.dll` tho
